From: Evan Doyle
To: Gabriel Fontes, Lucia Mendes
Subject: CAM Reconciliation Dispute – Tenant [Tenant Name]

Gabriel, Lucia,

We need to close the CAM reconciliation dispute for the tenant referenced in the subject line. I understand this issue has resurfaced, and we cannot let it linger further.

Please provide by end of business Friday:
- A line-item breakdown of disputed charges
- Supporting documentation for each disputed line item
- Your proposed resolution and any offset amounts

Once I have that, I will review and authorize a final settlement figure. I want a dated commitment from the tenant within two weeks of receipt.

If there are any blocking issues, flag them immediately so we can address them before the tenant escalates further.

Regards,
Evan Doyle
CFO, Stonebridge Property Group

---

From: Gabriel Fontes
To: Evan Doyle
Subject: RE: CAM Reconciliation Dispute – Tenant [Tenant Name]

Evan,

Thanks for the note. I have the line-item breakdown and supporting documentation ready for the disputed CAM charges, and I've flagged the key items below.

The dispute centers on three line items: snow removal (double-billed in January), common-area electrical (rate applied was from the prior contract), and a one-time landscaping charge that should have been amortized. The total disputed amount is $12,740, with $7,200 supported by corrected invoices and $5,540 requiring a manual adjustment.

Supporting documentation for each line item is compiled and can be shared immediately. My proposed resolution is to credit the full $12,740 against the tenant's next CAM statement, with no offset since the overcharges were our error.

I see no blocking issues on our side. I'll have the full package in your inbox by end of business Friday. Once you authorize the settlement figure, I'll coordinate the dated commitment letter for the tenant.

Please let me know if you want any adjustments before Friday.

Best,
Gabriel Fontes
Client Accounting Lead

---

From: Evan Doyle
To: Gabriel Fontes, Lucia Mendes
Subject: RE: CAM Reconciliation Dispute – Tenant [Tenant Name]

Gabriel, Lucia,

Gabriel, thank you for the summary. The proposed credit of $12,740 is clear, but I need the full package in my inbox by end of business Friday as stated. Include the corrected invoices for the $7,200 and the manual adjustment details for the $5,540.

I will review and authorize the settlement figure early next week. Once authorized, I expect a dated commitment from the tenant within two weeks of receipt. Lucia, please ensure the commitment letter template is ready and that we have a follow-up process in place if the tenant delays.

Flag anything that could block the timeline now—I want no surprises.

Regards,
Evan Doyle
CFO, Stonebridge Property Group

---

From: Evan Doyle
To: Gabriel Fontes, Lucia Mendes
Subject: RE: CAM Reconciliation Dispute – Tenant [Tenant Name] – Discrepancy in Figures

Gabriel, Lucia,

I've reviewed both of your emails, and there is a material discrepancy in the disputed amounts that must be resolved before I authorize any settlement. 

Gabriel cites a total disputed amount of $12,740 across three line items (snow removal, common-area electrical, and landscaping), with a proposed full credit of that amount. Lucia provides calculations for only two line items — janitorial services ($4,250) and landscaping ($2,875.50) — totaling $7,125.50, and recommends upholding both amounts with no offset. These cannot both be correct.

I need a single, reconciled breakdown by end of business Friday. Please align on which line items are actually in dispute, the correct dollar figures for each, and one proposed resolution. I will not sign off on a settlement number until I have a clear, consistent picture.

If there are any blockers to reconciling these numbers — whether documentation gaps or differing interpretations of the lease — flag them immediately.

Regards,
Evan Doyle
CFO, Stonebridge Property Group
